counterparty.name: Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI)
counterparty.role: Vendor providing site development, hosting, operation and maintenance services

missingRules.expectedFix: Add HDI indemnities for IP infringement, legal violations, Vendor-caused data breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct, with standard defense procedures and IP remedies.
missingRules.note: The Agreement contains no Vendor defense or indemnification obligation, including for third-party IP infringement claims.

missingRules.expectedFix: Require commercial general liability, workers' compensation, E&O and cyber/privacy insurance at the playbook limits, with certificates available on request.
missingRules.note: The hosting and development Vendor has no contractual insurance obligations.

missingRules.expectedFix: Require up to six months of transition assistance, data return in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter.
missingRules.note: The Agreement provides no post-termination transition assistance, Customer Data export or certified deletion process.

missingRules.expectedFix: Permit Company termination on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund and no more than a three-month fee, while limiting HDI convenience termination to a term end on 90 days' notice.
missingRules.note: The Company may terminate without cause on 90 days' notice, although the right is burdened by a potentially uncapped Termination Payment and HDI has the same right.

missingRules.expectedFix: Add warranties of professional and workmanlike performance, conformity to documentation, legal compliance and absence of malicious code, with repair, replacement or refund remedies.
missingRules.note: The corporate authority representations are not an express warranty covering service performance or conformity.

ourParty.name: The Deerskin Companies, Inc.
ourParty.role: Customer/client and owner of the Deerskin brand and Site content

spans.expectedFix: Require mutual written renewal or reduce the Customer's non-renewal notice to 30 days, and in all events no more than 60 days.
spans.note: The Agreement automatically renews for one-year terms with a 90-day opt-out window, exceeding the playbook's 60-day fallback maximum.

spans.expectedFix: Permit the Company to prevent renewal on no more than 60 days' notice, preferably 30 days with a Vendor reminder.
spans.note: The 90-day notice requirement for preventing renewal is longer than the acceptable 60-day fallback window.

spans.expectedFix: Add exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
spans.note: New York governing law is preferred, but the Agreement does not designate an exclusive dispute venue.

spans.expectedFix: Delete the Customer non-compete or narrowly limit it to named products for no more than 12 months with internal-development, acquisition and Vendor-performance carve-outs.
spans.note: The Company is barred during the term from participating in broadly defined similar Internet projects, without internal-development, acquisition or performance-failure carve-outs.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because the non-compete restricts only the Vendor.
spans.note: This restriction binds HDI, the Vendor, rather than the Company and therefore benefits the Customer.

spans.expectedFix: Remove the exclusivity or limit it to a defined category and 12 months, ending automatically upon HDI's failure to meet service or delivery obligations.
spans.note: The Company grants HDI exclusive online use of the Deerskin brand without a sufficient ongoing performance-based exit.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because the clause imposes no purchase commitment and protects the Customer against Vendor delay.
spans.note: This is not a Customer minimum commitment; it gives the Company a penalty-free termination right if HDI misses the launch deadline.

spans.expectedFix: Extend the access and use right to Company affiliates and contractors and make it transferable to an M&A successor, with termination only for uncured material breach.
spans.note: The Company's access and use right does not expressly cover affiliates, contractors acting on its behalf or M&A successors.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because the limited purpose license appropriately protects the Company's trademarks.
spans.note: The Company grants HDI only a narrow, non-exclusive license to use Company marks for performing the Agreement.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because the non-transferability limitation binds the Vendor, not the Customer.
spans.note: Non-transferability restricts HDI's ability to transfer the license to the Company's marks and therefore protects the Customer.

spans.expectedFix: Limit audits to once per 12 months by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, with no direct system access and costs borne by HDI absent a material underpayment.
spans.note: The audit has adequate notice, scope, timing and cost allocation, but it lacks an annual frequency cap and auditor confidentiality requirements.

spans.expectedFix: Add a mutual cap equal to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and $1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and the required uncapped carve-outs.
spans.note: This termination-payment formula is not a liability cap, and the Agreement contains no mutual aggregate cap or consequential-damages exclusion.

spans.expectedFix: Delete the termination payment or limit it to no more than three months' fees solely for Customer convenience termination, with no charge for HDI breach.
spans.note: The Company must pay a potentially substantial and uncapped termination charge based on annual Net Sales rather than a limited early-termination fee.
